Subject: Performance SLO & Private/VPC qualification - post-call recap

Hi Liam / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the thoughtful questions. Quick recap from our discovery and the next steps so we have alignment: 

- High-level goals: run Redwood Private (VPC) for ACME customer-facing API to meet 99.9% availability and P95 latency <= 120ms for 512-token generations.
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~120 qps across several model routes (text-gen + streaming chat).
- Concurrency/streams: 250 concurrent sessions with streaming enabled for low-latency token delivery; client-side will render tokens as they arrive.
- Networking constraints: customer prefers VPC peering but will also evaluate L3 VPN peering; egress IP allowlisting will be required.

Action items / next steps:
1) Aditya will validate network path options (VPC peering vs. IPsec VPN) and provide a checklist of required firewall rules, egress IPs, and MTU considerations.
2) ACME to share current NAT/egress topology and any proxied traffic patterns (Priya).
3) I will share the SLO questionnaire and a network diagram template.
4) We'll schedule a technical deep-dive next week with ACME infra and our infra team (propose Thu 11/19 or Fri 11/20).

Attachments: redwood-slo-questionnaire.xlsx (SLO targets / perf questions) and vpn-checklist.txt (initial reqs).

If anything above is off, flag and I'll update. Otherwise, please confirm the preferred deep-dive slot.

Thanks,

Marissa — thanks for the clear notes. Quick responses inline: 

- Targets look right. P95 <= 120ms is our initial target; if you have recommendations on per-route limits (e.g., chat vs. batch generation), happy to review.
- Throughput: 120 qps is accurate for peak. We may burst to ~200 qps for short windows (5–10 minutes).
- Concurrency/Streaming: streaming is a hard requirement for the chat UX. We need sub-100ms first-byte ideally, with steady token delivery thereafter.

Network side: Priya will pull our current egress/NAT diagram. We can support VPC peering in our primary cloud region (us-west-2). We also run a transit gateway with enforced egress proxies — will that affect peering?

Preferred deep-dive: Thu 11/19 morning PT works for our infra team.

Hi Liam / Priya — looping in some technical detail ahead of the deep-dive. TL;DR: VPC peering is ideal for latency but depends on your transit gateway/proxy architecture; IPsec VPN is supported but adds ~10–30ms overhead and can complicate streaming if MTU/tcp-mss isn't tuned.

Key points to validate on your side: 
- Egress & peering: if you can allow direct VPC peering between your VPC in us-west-2 and our Redwood Private VPC, that will minimize hops. If traffic must traverse a transit gateway with proxies, please list any L7 proxies or traffic inspection that will terminate long-lived connections.
- Keepalive & idle timeouts: streaming relies on stable long-lived connections; confirm any enforced idle timeouts (we recommend >= 5 minutes for token streaming sessions).
- MTU & fragmentation: ensure MTU >= 1400 across the path to avoid fragmentation with our gRPC/websocket streams.
- Egress IP allowlist: see attached acme-network-diagram.pdf for recommended IPs and ranges.
- Throughput testing: we suggest a staged perf test — start with 50 qps baseline, ramp to 120 qps, then a 200 qps burst test for 10 minutes. We'll instrument p95/p99 and first-byte latency.
- TLS termination: if you terminate TLS at the proxy, we need a passthrough option or mutual TLS for end-to-end.

Attachments: acme-network-diagram.pdf (stub) and a short vpn-checklist.txt with firewall ports and routes.

I'll be on the call Thu 11/19 09:30 PT. If you can share the transit gateway config and any proxy timeouts beforehand, that would help speed diagnostics.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Sr. Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
